paragraphs: The TCE is the voyage's freight less commission and voyage costs, divided by the days of the whole round voyage. It follows the Baltic Exchange's tanker method (Guide to Market Benchmarks v8.8, Appendix 3): the ship is delivered at the discharge port, Ningbo, sails in ballast to Galveston, loads, sails laden back and discharges. Steaming days carry a

weather margin; fuel is priced at the bunker port nearest the load port; port, waiting and canal days follow the route description. TD22 loads in the Galveston lightering area and sails laden round the Cape of Good Hope and through the Strait of Malacca to Ningbo, the strait the Baltic's own TD3C calculation takes with the same laden VLCC, rather than the shallower Sunda Strait of the shortest network line; in ballast it comes back through the Sunda Strait. The Baltic measures its distances on AtoBviaC tables, which are not published.
Operating and capital costs are not voyage costs: a TCE is compared with them, never net of them. A TCE without the ballast leg is a different number; the one here includes it.
formulas: TCE = (gross freight + other revenue - commission - voyage costs) / total voyage days
Voyage days = ballast steaming + laden steaming (each with the weather margin) + port, waiting and canal days
Freight that covers the voyage costs priced = voyage costs / (1 - commission share), the TCE set to zero

plain_verdict: A VLCC fixed on TD22, Galveston to Ningbo, at the Baltic's USD 58.22 million in the week to 23 October 2026, earns about USD 463,639 a day over a 111.1 day round voyage; freight of USD 17.34 a tonne would only cover the voyage costs priced.
